newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: RESEARCH ALERT - Pakistan Lever seen a buy.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Pakistan Lever seen a buy.

text.p: Pakistan Lever Brothers Ltd is seen as a buy on expectations of higher earnings in financial 1997/98 (July-June), a research report received on Friday said.
"Lever Brothers is the bluest of Pakistan's blue-chip stocks, with a dominating presence in the food and detergents markets," said the report by SocGen Crosby Securities.
"We recommend a buy for Lever Brothers' dividend yield and capital gains potential."

It said Lever Brothers' earnings were likely to remain stagnant in 1996/97 due to high levels of tea smuggling, but would jump 47 percent in 1997/98 thanks to reduced tarrifs and synergies. Earnings would rise another 38 percent the following year.

Lever Brothers and Brooke Bond Pakistan Ltd merged on May 19 and the combined company controls 45 percent of Pakistan's total packaged tea market. The synergies from the merger are expected to cut costs, SocGen Crosby said.
Brooke Bond, Pakistan's second largest producer of packaged tea, recorded sales of 4.2 billion rupees in 1996 and a net profit of 337 million rupees.

The report said Lever's merger with cash-rich Brooke Bond should improve dividends. "We expect dividends per share to increase by 50 percent in fiscal 1998 and a further 33 percent in 1999 for a dividend yield of 8.5 percent and 11.5 percent respectively."
Lever Brothers aggressively reduced prices of its products following recent tariff cuts to increase its market share.
In March, the government cut import tariffs to a maximum 45 percent from 65 percent, scrapped a 10 percent regulatory duty on imports and lowered sales tax to 12.5 percent from 18.

Lever Brothers responded by cutting its tea prices by up to 20 percent. SocGen Crosby said the company could now compete better against smuggled products, which would enable it to show strong volume growth.
Pakistan consumes about 140,000 tonnes of tea a year, roughly half of which is smuggled, the report said.
The combined tea operations of Lever Brothers and Brooke Bond constitute 45 percent of total tea sales and nearly 85 percent of the packaged tea market.
"This large volume gives the company an added clout in tea auctions as well as in negotiating shipping costs and should improve margins," the report said.
It said it assumed a 20 percent annual growth in Lever Brothers' detergents business due to price cuts.
The company's launch of its Walls brand ice-cream in Pakistan in 1995 had been one of the most successful product launches for the brand worldwide, the report added.
